text: Dish: يخنة الباذنجان بالرمان والجوز (Yakhnat al-Batinjan bil-Rumman wal-Jawz). A Levantine stew of fried eggplant braised in pomegranate molasses and a ground walnut-garlic sauce, finished with sumac and a tahini drizzle, typically served with rice or flatbread.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil.
Dish: Carrilleras de Cerdo al Pedro Ximénez con Puré de Boniato. Pork cheeks slow-braised in sweet Pedro Ximénez sherry until meltingly tender, served over a silky sweet potato purée.
Dish: Uni Shigureni Chazuke. Fresh sea urchin and simmered soy-ginger clams are laid over steamed rice, then bathed tableside in hot roasted-bonito dashi and scattered with nori and scallions.
Dish: Patty Melt.
Dish: Tourte de Canard aux Pruneaux et Armagnac. A golden, all-butter pastry pie encasing slow-braised duck leg, Armagnac-soaked prunes, and caramelized shallots, finished with a rich duck jus.

Dish: ต้มยำไก่กรอบใบมะกรูด. Crispy Kaffir-Lime Chicken Tom Yum -- pan-seared chicken thigh simmered in a fragrant tom yum broth of lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and roasted chili paste (nam prik pao), finished with fish sauce, lime juice, coconut milk, and crispy fried shallots.
Dish: ยำมะเขือยาวกุ้งสับ. A Thai charcoal-grilled long eggplant salad tossed with minced shrimp, shallots, bird's eye chili, lime juice, and fish sauce, finished with fresh cilantro.

Dish: Bún Riêu Ốc Bươu Đen. A Mekong Delta noodle soup built on a tangy tomato-crab broth loaded with black river snails and fried tofu, brightened with fresh herbs and a spoonful of fermented shrimp paste.
Dish: Callos a la Madrileña.
Dish: Char Siu.
Dish: Wu Gok Si Jing Pai Gwat. Steamed pork spare ribs tossed with crispy shredded taro, fermented black beans, and garlic, a classic Cantonese dim sum trolley favorite.
Dish: Spanakopita.
Dish: 灯影牛肉 (Dengying Beef).

Dish: سمبوسك الجبنة بالسماق والسمسم (Sambousek al-Jibneh bi'l-Summaq wa's-Simsim). Crescent-shaped pastries of thin wheat dough filled with tangy sumac-spiced akkawi cheese, sealed with an egg wash, rolled in toasted sesame seeds, and deep-fried until golden. Served hot with a garlic-tahini-yogurt dip.
Dish: Doro Wat.
Dish: Bún chả.
Dish: Kitfo.
Dish: Doro Zigni Firfir. Torn injera soaked in a fiery berbere-spiced chicken and hard-boiled egg stew, finished with a drizzle of spiced butter and served alongside tangy fresh ayib cheese.

Dish: Minestra di Ceci e Cozze alla Ligure. A Ligurian coastal soup of simmered chickpeas and mussels in a garlicky tomato-and-white-wine broth, finished with wild fennel and chili flakes, served with toasted crostini.
Dish: Route 9 Patty Melt. A juicy griddled beef patty layered with caramelized onions and melted Swiss cheese between two slices of grilled rye bread, served with crinkle-cut fries.
Dish: 冷吃兔 (Leng Chi Tu / Cold-Eaten Spicy Rabbit).
Dish: Musakhan. Palestinian roasted chicken slow-cooked with sumac and caramelized onions, served atop taboon flatbread drizzled with olive oil and scattered with toasted pine nuts.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Involtini di Melanzane alla Silana. Thin-sliced eggplant rolled around a filling of ricotta, provolone, and fresh mint, baked in a light tomato sugo and finished with toasted breadcrumbs.
Dish: Larb Moo.
Dish: Kibbeh Bil-Sanawbar. Crisp-fried shells of spiced lamb and freekeh wheat, stuffed with toasted pine nuts and sumac onions, served with a tahini-yogurt drizzle.
Dish: Haemul Pajeon.
Dish: Gaeng Kua Sapparod Goong. A tangy-sweet red curry simmered with juicy pineapple chunks, plump shrimp, and torn kaffir lime leaf for a bright, fragrant finish.

Dish: Fuqi Feipian (Sichuan Sliced Beef and Tripe in Chili Oil). Thin slices of poached beef shank and beef tripe tossed in a fiery Sichuan chili oil dressing with roasted peanuts, sesame seeds, and numbing peppercorns.
Dish: Musakhan. Palestinian roasted chicken piled high with caramelized sumac onions and toasted pine nuts, served over warm taboon flatbread soaked in olive oil.
Dish: Astakomanouri Santorinis. Chunks of lobster and creamy manouri cheese baked in a tomato-ouzo sauce, finished with a sesame-studded phyllo crust and fresh dill.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Pollo en Mole Verde de Pepita. Tender chicken thighs simmered in a vibrant green mole of toasted pumpkin seeds, tomatillos, jalapeño, cilantro, and epazote, served with warm corn tortillas.

Dish: 雪見鰤大根 (Yukimi Buri Daikon). Yellowtail simmered slowly with daikon radish in a soy, mirin, and sake broth until tender, served topped with a snowy mound of finely grated daikon and a touch of yuzu zest -- a winter dish evoking snow-viewing (yukimi).

Dish: Fregnacce Affumicate al Ragù Bianco di Cinghiale e Nocciole. Smoked, diamond-shaped fresh egg pasta ribbons from an Abruzzese-inspired tradition, tossed in a tomato-free white wild boar ragù finished with toasted hazelnuts and grated pecorino.
Dish: Kibbeh Sanieh bil-Laban. Layers of spiced ground lamb and cracked bulgur wheat baked golden in a tray, finished with a cooling garlic-mint yogurt sauce and toasted pine nuts.
Dish: Denver Omelette.
Dish: Mansaf.
Dish: Pla Neung Makrut Prik King. A whole fish gently steamed over kaffir lime leaves and galangal, then draped in a fiery red curry-chili paste brightened with fresh lime and garlic.

Dish: Tlacoyos de Requesón con Salsa de Chile Pasilla. Hand-shaped blue corn masa cakes stuffed with fresh requesón cheese, griddled until crisp, then topped with a smoky roasted pasilla chile salsa, crumbled queso fresco, and pickled nopales.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Blanquette de veau.

Dish: Route 9 Trucker's Hash Skillet. A cast-iron skillet piled with crispy hash browns, chopped bacon, griddled onions, and melted cheddar, topped with two eggs over easy and served with a side of buttered white toast.

Dish: 藤椒豌豆尖拌牛肚 (Téngjiāo Wāndòujiān Bàn Niúdǔ). A cold Sichuan appetizer of thinly sliced blanched beef tripe tossed with tender pea shoot greens, garlic, and a bright, numbing green Sichuan pepper (téngjiāo) oil dressing, finished with light soy sauce, a touch of sugar and vinegar, crushed toasted peanuts, and sesame seeds.

Dish: የጣና ሐይቅ አሳ ወጥ (Ye-Tana Haik Asa Wet). A berbere-spiced tilapia stew from the Lake Tana region, simmered in niter kibbeh (spiced clarified butter) with onions, garlic, ginger, and berbere, traditionally served atop injera.
Dish: Quenelles de Brochet Nantua. Delicate poached pike dumplings bound with butter and eggs, bathed in a creamy crayfish-studded Nantua sauce.

Dish: فريكة الحملان بالرمان (Fareekat al-Hamlan bil-Rumman). Slow-braised lamb shank served over smoky green freekeh wheat pilaf, finished with a tahini-yogurt sauce, toasted almonds and pine nuts, and a pomegranate molasses glaze with fresh pomegranate seeds.
Dish: Costillas de Cordero al Romero con Puré de Membrillo. Slow-roasted lamb ribs crusted with rosemary and garlic, served over a silky quince puree finished with a splash of sherry.
Dish: Quenelles de Brochet, Sauce Nantua. Delicate poached pike dumplings bound with choux pastry and eggs, bathed in a rich buttery crayfish cream sauce.
Dish: Doro Wat.

Dish: भरवा करेला (Bharwa Karela). Bitter gourd stuffed with a spiced filling of onions, crushed roasted peanuts, and ground coriander-fennel-amchur masala, pan-fried slowly in mustard oil until crisp; a classic North Indian home-style vegetable dish.

Dish: አሳ ክትፎ (Asa Kitfo). Finely minced Lake Tana tilapia gently warmed in niter kibbeh (spiced clarified butter) and berbere, served with ayib (fresh cottage cheese) and gomen (spiced collard greens) alongside injera.
Dish: Pla Sam Rot Makham. A whole crispy-fried fish is bathed in a glossy tamarind sauce balancing sweet, sour, and spicy notes, finished with fried garlic and crispy chilies.

Dish: 陳皮欖角蒸鯪魚球 (Chan Pei Laam Gok Jing Ling Yu Kau). Steamed dace fish balls, hand-beaten with pork fat and water chestnut for a springy bite, folded with aged tangerine peel and finely chopped preserved olive vegetable (欖角), then steamed and finished with a drizzle of hot oil, scallion, and light soy.
Dish: 海老柚子胡麻田楽 (Ebi Yuzu Goma Dengaku). Skewered shrimp grilled over charcoal and glazed with a sweet white miso-sesame sauce, finished with grated yuzu zest.

Dish: كبة السماق بالرمان (Kibbet Summaq bil Rumman). Torpedo-shaped kibbeh shells of fine bulgur and minced lamb, stuffed with a filling of spiced ground lamb, toasted walnuts, sumac, and pomegranate molasses, then deep-fried until crisp; served with a tangy yogurt-tahini dip.
Dish: Patty Melt.

Dish: Tarte Fine aux Poireaux, Anchois et Noisettes du Périgord. A delicate open-faced tart of buttery pastry topped with melted leeks, salted anchovy fillets, and toasted Périgord hazelnuts, finished with a drizzle of hazelnut oil.
Dish: Dongchimi Memil-jeon. A crisp buckwheat pancake studded with scallions and pan-fried, served alongside a chilled cup of tangy dongchimi (radish water kimchi) broth for dipping and sipping.

Dish: কাঁঠালের কোফতা কারি (Kathaler Kofta Curry). A Bengali vegetarian curry of golden-fried jackfruit-and-potato dumplings (kofta), bound with gram flour and simmered in a mustard-oil gravy enriched with cashew-poppy seed paste, ginger, and garam masala.
Dish: Vitello Tonnato.
Dish: Buta no Kakuni.

Dish: Route 9 Trucker's Hash. A mountain of crispy skillet home fries smothered in melted cheddar, diced smoked ham, caramelized onions, and two eggs any style, finished with a ladle of house country gravy.
Dish: Kkotge Doenjang-jjigae. A robust Korean stew of whole blue crab simmered in fermented soybean paste with zucchini, tofu, and scallions, served bubbling hot alongside steamed rice.
Dish: Char Siu.

Dish: Shuizhu Niurou (水煮牛肉). Paper-thin slices of beef are poached in a blistering broth of dried chilies, Sichuan peppercorns, and garlic, then ladled over crisp bean sprouts and blanketed in a final cascade of smoking hot chili oil.

Dish: Chuckwagon Skillet Slam. A cast-iron diner skillet of crispy hash browns, griddled ground beef, onions, and bell peppers smothered in melted cheddar and country gravy, topped with two eggs cooked to order.
Dish: Adam and Eve on a Raft, Wreck 'Em. Diner slang for two eggs scrambled and served on a slice of buttered toast -- a classic short-order breakfast plate.
Dish: Shui Zhu Niu Rou. Tender beef slices poached in a fiery, oil-slicked Sichuan broth loaded with dried chilies and numbing Sichuan peppercorns.
Dish: Bún riêu cua.
Dish: Pad Kra Pao Moo.

Dish: Mixiotes de Conejo en Adobo de Chile Puya. Rabbit pieces marinated in a smoky-tangy adobo of toasted chile puya, garlic, cumin, and vinegar, wrapped in a maguey (agave) leaf membrane and steamed until tender -- a specialty of the central Mexican highlands (Hidalgo/Puebla region). Translation: 'Rabbit maguey-parchment bundles in chile puya adobo.'.

Dish: Blue Plate Meatloaf Melt. A diner blue-plate special of housemade beef-and-pork meatloaf smothered in brown onion gravy and melted cheddar, served open-faced on white toast with a side of buttery mashed potatoes.
Dish: Pad Kra Pao Gai.

Dish: 欖角豉汁蒸大眼雞 (Laam Gok Sih Zap Zing Daai Ngaan Gai). A whole bulgy-eye fish (大眼雞) steamed on the bone with fermented black beans, minced preserved olive (欖角), julienned ginger and scallion, then finished with a sizzle of hot oil and a light drizzle of soy - a punchy, salty-savoury Cantonese steamed-fish preparation.
Dish: Shakshuka.
Dish: Blanquette de veau.
Dish: Braciole alla Napoletana. Thin beef rolls stuffed with breadcrumbs, pecorino, pine nuts, raisins, garlic, and parsley, then slow-braised in a rich tomato sauce.

Dish: Θαλασσόπιτα Καστελλόριζου (Thalassópita Kastellórizou). A savory phyllo pie from the island of Kastellorizo, layered with flaked local grouper, wild horta (foraged greens), mizithra cheese, and a wash of olive oil, finished with a sprinkle of sesame seeds on the top crust.
Dish: Pasta alla Norma.
Dish: Agujjim.
Dish: Pastitsio.
Dish: Songi-beoseot Yangnyeom Jeon. A crispy pan-seared pancake of matsutake mushrooms bound with egg and rice flour, finished with a sweet-savory soy-sesame glaze and scattered scallions.

Dish: Bún Mắm Nêm Cá Lóc Nướng Trui. Rice vermicelli topped with whole snakehead fish grilled over straw fire, torn into flakes and served with pungent fermented anchovy sauce (mắm nêm), roasted peanuts, pickled green papaya, and a platter of fresh herbs.
Dish: Sega Awaze Tibs. Cubes of pan-seared beef tossed in a fiery awaze sauce of berbere chili paste, garlic, and rosemary, served sizzling with injera.

Dish: The Hobo's Sunrise Skillet (diner slang, meaning: 'a scramble of whatever's on hand, served hot for breakfast'). A cast-iron skillet of crispy hash browns, scrambled eggs, crumbled breakfast sausage, sauteed onions and peppers, melted cheddar, and country sausage gravy, topped with a buttermilk biscuit on the side.

Dish: 감자명란부침개 (Gamja Myeongnan Buchimgae). A savory Korean pan-fried pancake made from grated potato and salted pollock roe (myeongnan), bound with egg and flour, cooked in sesame oil until crisp, and served with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

Dish: فريكة بالدجاج والصنوبر (Farikeh bil Dajaj wal Sonobar). A Levantine one-pot pilaf of smoky roasted green wheat (freekeh) simmered in spiced chicken broth, topped with tender braised chicken, golden toasted pine nuts and slivered almonds, and finished with a drizzle of samna (clarified butter).

Dish: 花椒松茸炖土鸡 (Huājiāo Sōngróng Dùn Tǔjī). Free-range chicken slow-braised with fresh matsutake mushrooms, Sichuan peppercorns, ginger, scallion, and Shaoxing wine -- a fragrant, numbing mountain-style braise from Sichuan's forested border counties.
Dish: 金瓜蟹肉扒豆腐 (Golden Pumpkin & Crab Meat Braised Tofu). Silky egg tofu and sweet steamed pumpkin gently braised in a light crab meat and egg white gravy, finished with a drizzle of scallion oil.
Dish: Pla Duk Foo Yum Mamuang. Crispy deep-fried shredded catfish piled high and served with a tangy-spicy green mango salad tossed in lime, chili, and fish sauce.
Dish: Doro Wat.

Dish: ምስር ክትፎ በጤልባ ዘይት (Misir Kitfo be Telba Zeyt). A vegan reinterpretation of kitfo: red lentils are simmered until tender, then mashed and warmed with berbere, a pinch of fiery mitmita, minced garlic and ginger, and finished with nutty cold-pressed flaxseed oil (telba zeyt) in place of spiced butter. Served mounded on injera, traditionally with a side of fresh ayib cheese and sautéed collard greens (gomen).
Dish: Cochinita Pibil.
Dish: Bánh Xèo Tôm Thịt Nướng Than. A crispy turmeric rice-flour pancake filled with charcoal-grilled shrimp, pork belly, and bean sprouts, wrapped in lettuce and herbs and dipped in tangy nuoc cham.
Dish: Patty Melt.
Dish: Asa Tibs Bahir Dar. Pan-seared Lake Tana tilapia tossed with berbere, garlic, and rosemary in spiced niter kibbeh butter, served sizzling alongside injera.
Dish: Bhagara Baingan. Baby eggplants simmered whole in a roasted peanut, sesame, and tamarind gravy, a classic Hyderabadi specialty often served at weddings and festive meals.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil.
Dish: Sultani Kibbeh bil-Sanieh. A copper tray of baked bulgur-and-lamb kibbeh layered with spiced minced beef and pine nuts, finished with a tart pomegranate-tahini glaze.
Dish: Nihari. A slow-braised Lucknowi stew of bone-in mutton shank simmered overnight with garam masala and wheat-flour thickening, finished with fried ginger, green chili, and a squeeze of lime.
Dish: Musakhan.

Dish: Konkani Kokum Batata Rassa. A ruby-hued Konkan coastal curry of baby potatoes simmered in a tangy kokum-tamarind coconut broth, finished with a crackling tempering of mustard seeds and curry leaves.

Dish: Ham Daan Jing Yuk Beng (Steamed Minced Pork with Salted Duck Egg). A silky patty of hand-chopped minced pork steamed until just set beneath a whole salted duck egg, its savory juices mingling into a pool perfect for spooning over steamed rice.
Dish: Rogan Josh.
Dish: Malfouf Mahshi bi Lahm w Rumman. Tender cabbage leaves rolled around spiced lamb and rice, simmered in a tangy pomegranate-tomato broth and served with a dollop of garlicky yogurt.

Dish: 金銀蒜蒸蝦滑釀節瓜 (Gām Ngán Syun Jīng Hā Waat Yeuhng Jit Gwā). Fuzzy melon segments hollowed and stuffed with hand-minced fresh shrimp paste, steamed and topped with a mix of golden (fried) and silver (raw) garlic, finished with a light soy-oyster glaze and scallion oil.
Dish: Kotopoulo Riganato Karpathou. Bone-in chicken thighs slow-roasted in a clay pot with potatoes, wild oregano, lemon, and Karpathian olive oil.

Dish: Tamal de Frijol Negro y Chapulines. A Oaxacan-style corn masa tamal filled with spiced black beans and toasted chapulines (grasshoppers), wrapped in a corn husk and steamed, traditionally served with a smear of crema and salsa.
Dish: Miner's Skillet Hash. A cast-iron skillet piled with crispy home fries, chopped ham, grilled peppers and onions, smothered in melted cheddar and topped with two eggs any style.
Dish: Pad Thai.
Dish: Oyakodon.

Dish: Conejo en Adobo Serrano. Wild rabbit slow-braised in a smoky adobo of toasted guajillo and pasilla chiles, garlic, and epazote, served with warm blue corn tortillas in the style of the Tlaxcala highlands.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil.
Dish: Rogan Josh.
Dish: Musakhan.

Dish: كبة السماق والرمان (Kibbat al-Summaq wa al-Rumman). Baked bulgur-wheat kibbeh shells stuffed with spiced minced lamb, walnuts, and pine nuts, glazed with pomegranate molasses and sumac, served over a tahini-yogurt sauce and garnished with toasted sesame and pomegranate seeds.
Dish: Bánh Xèo.

Dish: 명란 들기름 비빔국수 (Myeongnan Deulgireum Bibim-guksu). Chilled wheat noodles tossed in nutty perilla oil and soy sauce, topped with salted pollock roe (myeongnan), a soft egg, crumbled seaweed, and sesame seeds.

Dish: Κουνέλι Στιφάδο με Μαστίχα Χίου και Κυδώνι (Rabbit Stifado with Chios Mastic and Quince). A slow-braised wild rabbit stew from the Aegean tradition, simmered with pearl onions, ripe tomato, red wine, warming spices (cinnamon, clove, bay), quince wedges, and a whisper of Chios mastic resin for a resinous, floral finish.

Dish: Χοιρινό Πηλού με Δαμάσκηνα και Καρύδια (Choirinó Piloú me Damáskina kai Karýdia). Pork shoulder slow-baked in a sealed clay pot with prunes, walnuts, onions, red wine, cinnamon, and honey -- a rustic Macedonian-style braise served with its own syrupy pan juices.
Dish: Tourte aux escargots et noisettes en beurre persillé. A rustic Burgundian double-crust pastry pie filled with escargots, toasted hazelnuts, garlic, and parsley butter.

Dish: لفائف الفريكة باللحم والصنوبر (Lafā'if al-Freekeh bil-Laḥm wa'l-Ṣanawbar). Vine leaves wrapped around smoky roasted freekeh (cracked green wheat) mixed with minced lamb, toasted pine nuts, allspice and cinnamon, simmered in a tamarind-tomato broth, then finished with a drizzle of tahini-yogurt sauce and a scatter of toasted sesame seeds.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Sarde a Beccafico. Sicilian sardines butterflied and rolled around a filling of toasted breadcrumbs, pine nuts, raisins, and orange zest, then baked with a drizzle of olive oil until golden.

Dish: Musakhan. Palestinian roasted chicken marinated in tangy sumac and cooked with mountains of caramelized onions, served atop olive-oil-soaked taboon flatbread and scattered with toasted pine nuts.

Dish: كبة السمك بالطحينة والرمان (Kibbet as-Samak bil-Tahina wal-Rumman). A coastal Levantine baked kibbeh: a bulgur-wheat shell filled with spiced flaked fish, caramelized onions, and toasted walnuts, baked until golden and finished with a tahini-lemon sauce and a drizzle of pomegranate molasses.
Dish: Soutzoukakia Smyrneika. Cumin-spiced beef and breadcrumb meatballs simmered in a red wine tomato sauce, a Smyrna-style classic often served over rice or orzo.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil. Slow-roasted pork marinated in tangy achiote paste and sour orange juice, wrapped in banana leaves and pit-roasted until meltingly tender, then served with pickled red onions.
Dish: Rogan Josh.

Dish: Nem Nướng Sả Ớt Miền Trung. Central Vietnamese grilled pork skewers pounded with lemongrass and chili, charred over coals and wrapped in rice paper with herbs, served with a peanut dipping sauce.
Dish: Sundubu-jjigae.
Dish: Tortelli di Zucca e Amaretti al Burro Salviato. Handmade pumpkin tortelli stuffed with roasted squash and crushed amaretti, tossed in nutty brown butter with crisped sage leaves.

Dish: አሳ በቆሎ ወጥ (Asa Beqolo Wet). A Lake Tana-style Ethiopian fish stew: firm freshwater fish simmered in a berbere and niter kibbeh (spiced clarified butter) sauce with onions, garlic, and ginger, thickened with ground roasted barley (qolo), served with injera.
Dish: Chettinad Kozhi Varuval. Bite-sized chicken pieces dry-roasted with black pepper, curry leaves, and a fiery hand-ground Chettinad spice blend until deeply caramelized.
Dish: Jeonbok Naengchae. Chilled abalone slices tossed with julienned pear, cucumber, and pine nuts in a tangy gochujang-vinegar dressing.
Dish: Fabada Asturiana.
Dish: Wonton Noodle Soup.

Dish: Malfouf bi Freekeh w Rumman. Tender cabbage leaves rolled around smoky freekeh and spiced lamb, gently simmered in a tangy pomegranate-molasses broth and finished with toasted pine nuts and mint.

Dish: কাঁঠালের কোফতা কারি (Kathaler Kofta Kari). A Bengali dish of grated raw jackfruit and spiced potato shaped into deep-fried dumplings (kofta), simmered in a cashew-onion gravy tempered with panch phoron and mustard oil.
Dish: Freekeh Djaj Mfarraket. Shredded slow-braised chicken folded through smoky roasted green wheat freekeh with caramelized onions, toasted almonds, and a whisper of cinnamon.

Dish: แกงคั่วหอยขมใบชะพลู (Gaeng Khua Hoi Khom Bai Cha Phlu). A southern Thai-style curry of river trumpet snails simmered in a red curry paste of dried chilies, shrimp paste, and coconut milk, finished with wild betel leaves and fingerroot for a peppery, aromatic bite.
Dish: White Cut Chicken (白切雞).

Dish: Chiles en Nogada. A roasted poblano pepper stuffed with a sweet-savory picadillo of shredded pork, beef, apples, pears, and plantains, battered and fried, then blanketed in a creamy walnut sauce and finished with pomegranate seeds and parsley.
Dish: Khao Soi Gai.
Dish: Char Siu.
Dish: Larb Moo.

Dish: 藤椒仔姜爆炒鳝丝 (Téngjiāo Zǐjiāng Bàochǎo Shànsī). A Sichuan home-style stir-fry of julienned live eel (huangshan) flash-fried over high heat with young ginger shreds, garlic, scallion, and a heavy dose of fresh green Sichuan pepper (téngjiāo) for a bright, tingling numbness rather than red-chili heat. The eel is briefly velveted in egg white and cornstarch, then finished with soy sauce, a splash of Shaoxing wine, and a dab of doubanjiang for depth, with a final drizzle of sesame oil.

Dish: Fideuà de Marisco. A Valencian noodle dish where short toasted fideos are simmered in a saffron-infused fish and shellfish stock alongside prawns, mussels, and squid, finished with a dollop of garlicky allioli.
Dish: Spaghetti alla Carbonara.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Adam and Eve on a Raft, Wreck 'Em. Classic American diner short-order slang for two eggs scrambled and served on buttered toast, plated with crispy hash browns and a side of bacon.
Dish: Doro Zilzil Awaze. Strips of pan-seared chicken breast tossed in a fiery awaze chili-garlic paste and spiced niter kibbeh, piled onto warm injera.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil.

Dish: كبة الرمان والصنوبر (Kibbet al-Rumman wal-Sonobar). Torpedo-shaped bulgur-wheat shells filled with spiced minced lamb, toasted pine nuts, and pomegranate molasses, deep-fried and served with a tahini-yogurt dipping sauce.
Dish: Chicken Chettinad.
Dish: Arni Youvetsi tis Kyra-Popis. Slow-braised lamb shanks baked in a clay pot with orzo, tomato, and cinnamon, finished with a blanket of melted kefalotyri cheese.

Dish: Rape en Salsa Verde con Almejas. A Basque coastal dish of monkfish medallions and clams gently poached in a garlicky green sauce made with parsley, white wine, and olive oil, thickened lightly with flour.

Dish: ลาบปลาดุกกรอบใบมะกรูด (Lap Pla Duk Krop Bai Makrut). Crispy fried catfish flaked and tossed Isaan-style with toasted rice powder, shallots, mint, kaffir lime leaf, lime juice, fish sauce, and dried chili flakes.
Dish: Fagottini di Baccalà alla Ligure. Thin egg-pasta parcels filled with salt cod, pine nuts, Taggiasca olives, garlic, parsley, and breadcrumbs, baked in white wine with a drizzle of olive oil.
Dish: Har Gow.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil. Slow-roasted achiote-marinated pork wrapped in banana leaves, traditionally pit-cooked and served with pickled red onions in warm corn tortillas.
Dish: Blue Plate Smothered Hash Skillet. Crispy skillet hash browns topped with two eggs any style, melted cheddar, sausage gravy, and scallions.
Dish: Doro Wat.

Dish: Cà Ri Nghêu Lá É (Phú Yên). A Central Vietnamese clam curry from Phú Yên province, simmering fresh nghêu (clams) in a light turmeric-lemongrass-coconut broth with lá é (hoary basil) and fresh chili, typically served with crusty bread or rice vermicelli for dipping.
Dish: Kibbet Sanieh bil Loz. A tray-baked kibbeh of spiced bulgur and minced lamb, layered with a rich filling and finished with toasted almonds, pine nuts, and a drizzle of pomegranate molasses.

Dish: The Slinger's Sunrise Skillet. A Rust Belt diner classic: crispy hash browns smothered in beef chili, blanketed with melted cheddar, topped with two fried eggs, diced onion, and pickled jalapeños, served with a side of buttered white toast.
Dish: Soutzoukakia.

Dish: 전복내장된장찌개 (Jeonbok-naejang Doenjang-jjigae). A hearty Jeju Island stew made by simmering abalone innards with doenjang (fermented soybean paste), radish, zucchini, and tofu in an anchovy-based broth.
Dish: Quenelles de brochet.

Dish: Ruby's Route 9 Meatloaf Melt. An open-faced beef meatloaf sandwich on grilled Texas toast, smothered in brown gravy and melted cheddar, finished with a swipe of horseradish-mustard aioli and served with mashed potatoes -- a classic roadside American diner plate.
Dish: Agujjim (아귀찜). Monkfish and bean sprouts braised in a fiery garlic-gochujang sauce, finished with sesame seeds and scallions.
Dish: Larb Moo.
Dish: Kua Kling Goong Sapparot. A fiery Southern Thai dry-curry stir-fry of shrimp and sweet pineapple in a hand-pounded paste of lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaf, and bird's eye chilies.
Dish: Awash Zilzil Wot. Thin-sliced beef simmered low and slow in a smoky berbere sauce, finished with spiced niter kibbeh butter and served over injera.
Dish: Chicken Fried Steak.
Dish: Dan Dan Mian.
Dish: Har Cheung Fun (蝦腸粉). Silky steamed rice noodle rolls filled with fresh whole shrimp, served glistening with a drizzle of light soy sauce and sesame oil.

Dish: Empanadillas de Chipirones en su Tinta. Small crescent-shaped pastries from the Andalusian coast, filled with baby squid stewed in their own ink with onion, garlic, and a splash of oloroso sherry, then sealed with an egg wash and fried until golden.
Dish: Blue Plate Meatloaf Special. Slow-baked beef meatloaf smothered in tomato-brown gravy, served with buttery mashed potatoes and glazed carrots.

Dish: ઊંધિયું (Undhiyu). A layered Gujarati winter mixed-vegetable dish combining purple yam, sweet potato, eggplant, green beans, and banana with spiced muthiya (fenugreek-and-gram-flour dumplings), traditionally slow-cooked upside down in an earthen pot buried in the ground.
Dish: Chtapodokeftedes Santorinis. Crispy pan-fried fritters of tender braised octopus folded into a creamy fava bean puree with capers, red onion, and oregano, finished with a squeeze of lemon.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Tourte forestière au Comté et noisettes. A golden butter-pastry pie filled with wild mushrooms, melted Comté cheese, and toasted hazelnuts, finished with a splash of dry white wine.

Dish: 陳皮鴨腎蒸肉餅 (Chan Pei Aap Sun Jing Yuk Beng). A classic Cantonese home-style steamed dish: minced pork patty studded with diced dried duck gizzard and rehydrated aged tangerine peel (chan pei), seasoned with soy sauce, sesame oil and ginger, then steamed until firm and served in its own savoury juices.
Dish: Fabada Asturiana.

Dish: 豉椒炒花蟹 (Sih Jīu Cháau FāHáaih). Live flower crab wok-tossed with fermented black beans, garlic, ginger, and sliced red chilies in a light soy-based sauce, served Cantonese-style over the shell for extra flavor absorption.

Dish: 梅菜叉燒煎堆 (Mui Choi Char Siu Jin Deui). Deep-fried glutinous rice balls coated in sesame seeds, filled with a sweet-savoury mix of char siu (barbecued pork) and preserved mustard greens (mui choi) -- a modern Cantonese dim sum twist on the classic sesame ball.

Dish: Route 9 Denver Skillet. A cast-iron skillet of diced ham, peppers, and onions folded into three scrambled eggs with melted cheddar, piled over crispy hash browns and served with buttered rye toast.

Dish: The Crossroads Reuben Melt. Grilled marble rye piled high with slow-braised corned beef, tangy sauerkraut, melted Swiss, and a swipe of Thousand Island dressing, pressed on the flat-top until golden.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil. Slow-roasted achiote-marinated pork wrapped in banana leaves, traditionally from Yucatán and served with pickled red onions and warm corn tortillas.
Dish: Gaeng Massaman Gai.
Dish: Mapo Doufu.

Dish: 새우젓갈비찜 (Saeujeot-galbijjim). Beef short ribs slow-braised in soy sauce, garlic, Asian pear, and a spoonful of salted fermented shrimp (saeujeot) for deep umami, finished with sesame oil, sesame seeds, and pine nuts.
Dish: Doro Wat.
Dish: Qīngchéng Málà Jī Dīng. Diced chicken thigh wok-tossed with roasted peanuts, dried chilies, and Sichuan peppercorns in a tangy, numbing doubanjiang glaze.

Dish: 도라지 유자 강정 (Doraji Yuja Gangjeong). Thin batons of bellflower root (doraji) deep-fried until crisp, then tossed in a sticky honey-yuzu glaze and finished with toasted sesame seeds and pine nuts; served as a sweet-tart banchan or tea-time snack.

Dish: Γιουβέτσι με Χταπόδι (Octopus Giouvetsi -- octopus and orzo pasta baked in a tomato-wine sauce, topped with grated hard cheese). A Greek clay-pot dish of tender octopus slow-braised in a tomato and red wine sauce, baked together with kritharaki (orzo) pasta until the pasta soaks up the sauce, finished with grated kefalotyri or graviera cheese.
Dish: Soutzoukakia.
Dish: Patty Melt.

Dish: Zheng Ham Daan Ham Yue Yuk Beng (Steamed Minced Pork with Salted Egg and Dried Shrimp). A home-style Cantonese steamed pork patty studded with rich salted duck egg and dried shrimp, finished with fresh ginger and scallion over the savory pan juices.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil.
Dish: Zilzil Awaze Tibs. Strips of tender beef sautéed in spiced niter kibbeh butter and fiery awaze chili paste, served sizzling atop torn injera.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Coq au Vin.

Dish: अखरोट भरवां वांगुन (Akhrot Bharwan Wangun). Kashmiri baby eggplants slit and stuffed with a spiced walnut-paneer paste, shallow-fried in mustard oil, then simmered in a yogurt gravy tempered with mustard seeds, asafoetida, fennel, and dry ginger powder.

Dish: Μελιτζανοκεφτέδες Νησιώτικοι με Ανθότυρο και Κάππαρη. Island-style eggplant fritters from the Aegean, made with roasted eggplant, soft anthotyro cheese, capers, and fresh herbs, pan-fried until golden and served with a drizzle of lemon.

Dish: Fazzoletti di Seta al Pesto di Noci di Portofino. Thin, square sheets of fresh egg pasta ('silk handkerchiefs') from the Ligurian coast, folded loosely and dressed with a creamy walnut-and-marjoram pesto enriched with Parmigiano and a touch of cream, finished with cracked walnuts and lemon zest.
Dish: Kibbeh Nayyeh bi Snawbar. Hand-pounded raw lamb blended with fine bulgur, onion, and Aleppo pepper, mounded on a platter, topped with toasted pine nuts and a drizzle of olive oil.

Dish: Fagottini di Baccalà e Farro con Salsa alle Nocciole. Small dumplings of salt cod and mashed potato wrapped in a spelt-flour shell, poached and served with a brown butter and toasted hazelnut sauce, finished with parsley and lemon zest.
Dish: Pastitsio.
Dish: Croquetas de Jamón Ibérico y Piñones al Romero. Crisp, golden croquettes filled with a silky béchamel, hand-shredded Ibérico ham, and toasted pine nuts, perfumed with a touch of fresh rosemary.

Dish: তিল বাদাম কাঁকড়া কারি (Til-Badam Kankra Curry). A coastal Bengali crab curry from the Sundarbans delta region, where crab is simmered in a paste of ground sesame seeds and almonds, mustard oil, mustard paste, and whisked yogurt, finished with a ghee-and-nigella-seed tempering and served over steamed rice.

Dish: Nem Nướng Ống Tre Bà Ba. Smoky grilled pork sausage skewers, traditionally smoked inside bamboo tubes, served with rice paper, fresh herbs, pickled vegetables, and a tangy peanut-hoisin dipping sauce.

Dish: Camarones en Salsa de Pipián Rojo con Ajonjolí Tostado. Gulf shrimp simmered in a toasted pumpkin-seed and dried chile sauce (pipián rojo), finished with a generous sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and served with warm corn tortillas.

Dish: Adam and Eve on a Raft, Wreck 'Em (diner lingo) -- "Two poached eggs on toast, scrambled instead". Classic American diner short-order slang dish: buttered toast topped with eggs scrambled to order, a staple of mid-century soda-fountain and diner counters where cooks and waitstaff communicated orders in coded lingo.

Dish: The Hobo Skillet (Loaded Hash Browns with Country Gravy). A cast-iron diner skillet of crispy hash browns loaded with bacon, breakfast sausage, sauteed onions and peppers, two eggs any style, melted cheddar, and smothered in peppery country sausage gravy, served with buttered toast on the side.
Dish: Haemul Sundubu-Jjigae. A bubbling, fiery red stew of silky soft tofu, mixed shellfish, and gochugaru broth, served still boiling in its stone pot with a raw egg cracked on top.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil.

Dish: كبة حامض بالسلق والرمان (Kibbet Hamod bis-Silq wa'r-Rumman). An Iraqi soul-soup: bulgur-and-minced-lamb kibbeh dumplings stuffed with a walnut-onion filling, simmered in a tangy broth of Swiss chard, pomegranate molasses, garlic, and dried mint.

Dish: Fúqī Fèngwěi Piàn (Husband-and-Wife Phoenix-Tail Slices). Thin-sliced poached chicken and chicken skin tossed in a glossy Sichuan chili oil with crushed roasted peanuts, scallions, and numbing Sichuan peppercorn, a reimagined Chengdu street-food classic.

Dish: كبة السمك بالطحينة (Kibbet as-Samak bil-Tahina). Torpedo-shaped kibbeh shells of bulgur wheat and minced white fish, stuffed with spiced onions, pine nuts, and parsley, then fried and served with a lemon-tahini sauce.

Dish: Mextlapique de Acamayas en Hoja Santa. Freshwater river prawns from Veracruz's Papaloapan basin, seasoned with garlic, epazote, and a guajillo-tomato salsa, then wrapped in hoja santa leaves and corn husks and grilled over charcoal until the leaves char and perfume the prawns.
Dish: Fabada Asturiana.

Dish: Wok-Seared Beef with Bitter Melon in Black Bean Sauce. Tender flank beef and blanched bitter melon are flash-fried in a fragrant garlic and fermented black bean sauce, finished with a splash of Shaoxing wine.
Dish: Larb Pla Salmon Rom Fai. Smoky seared salmon flaked and tossed with toasted rice powder, chili, shallots, lime juice, and fresh mint in the style of Northeastern Thai larb.

Dish: كُبَّة الفريكة بالقشطة والرمان (Kubbat al-Freekeh bil-Qishta wal-Rumman). Fried torpedo-shaped shells of spiced freekeh and bulgur stuffed with minced lamb, sautéed onions, and toasted pine nuts, served over a pool of qishta (clotted cream), drizzled with pomegranate molasses, and finished with toasted sesame seeds and sumac.

Dish: 깻잎새우전 (Kkaennip Saeu-jeon). Perilla leaves stuffed with a seasoned minced shrimp filling, dusted in flour, dipped in beaten egg, and pan-fried until golden; served with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce.
Dish: Saba no Misoni.
Dish: Jjajangmyeon.
Dish: Denver Omelette.

Dish: Bún Sứa Nắng Hạ. A coastal Vietnamese noodle soup (translation: 'Summer Sunshine Jellyfish Noodle Soup') featuring crunchy jellyfish, poached shrimp, and rice vermicelli in a sweet-sour tamarind and fish sauce broth, topped with herbs, bean sprouts, and fried shallots.

Dish: Mixiotes de Conejo en Adobo de Chile Pasilla y Hoja de Aguacate. Rabbit pieces marinated in a smoky adobo of toasted pasilla and guajillo chiles, garlic, and avocado leaf, wrapped in parchment-steamed maguey-leaf paper (mixiote) and slow-steamed until tender; served with charred corn tortillas.
Dish: Bún riêu cua.

Dish: Camarones en Costra de Pepita con Salsa de Chile Pasilla (Pumpkin-Seed-Crusted Shrimp in Pasilla Chile Sauce). Gulf shrimp coated in a toasted ground pepita (pumpkin seed) crust, pan-seared, and served over a silky roasted pasilla chile and tomato sauce, finished with a drizzle of Mexican crema and queso fresco.
Dish: Rogan Josh.
Dish: Gongura Mutton. A tangy Andhra-style curry of tender mutton simmered with sour gongura (sorrel) leaves, garlic, and red chilies until deeply spiced and fragrant.

Dish: ตำมะยมกุ้งแห้ง (Tam Mayom Kung Haeng). A pounded Thai salad made from tart star gooseberries, dried shrimp, garlic, bird's eye chilies, palm sugar, and fish sauce, finished with roasted peanuts -- a sour-spicy-salty dish in the tradition of som tam.
Dish: Bagara Baingan.
Dish: Musakhan.
Dish: Sundubu-jjigae.

Dish: 红油耳丝拌折耳根 (Hóngyóu Ěrsī Bàn Zhé'ěrgēn). A cold Sichuan appetizer of thinly sliced braised pig ear tossed with fresh houttuynia root (fish-mint), chili oil, Sichuan peppercorn, garlic, and scallion.
Dish: Doro Wat.
Dish: Dhaniya Murgh Handi. Chicken pieces slow-simmered in a fresh coriander-yogurt gravy with charred onions, green chilies, and toasted cumin, finished in a clay handi for a smoky, tangy depth.
Dish: Buri Daikon. Yellowtail and daikon radish slowly simmered together in a sweet-savory broth of soy sauce, sake, mirin, and sugar, a beloved winter comfort dish.

Dish: حمام محشي بالفريكة والصنوبر واللوز (Hamam Mahshi bil-Freekeh was-Sanawbar wal-Lawz). Whole squab (young pigeon) stuffed with spiced smoked green-wheat freekeh, toasted pine nuts, and almonds, slow-roasted and finished with a pomegranate molasses glaze.

Dish: Tamal de Camarón en Adobo de Chile Ancho envuelto en Hoja de Plátano. A coastal Oaxacan-style tamale of fresh shrimp bathed in a deep-red ancho chile adobo, folded into corn masa and steamed inside a banana leaf for a smoky, earthy aroma.

Dish: كبة الرمان بالصنوبر واللبن (Kubbat al-Rumman bil-Sanawbar wal-Laban). Torpedo-shaped shells of fine bulgur wheat stuffed with spiced minced lamb, toasted pine nuts, and pomegranate molasses, deep-fried until crisp and served drizzled with garlicky tahini-yogurt sauce and fresh pomegranate seeds.

Dish: 帆立と舞茸の利休胡麻味噌鍋 (Hotate to Maitake no Rikyū Goma Miso Nabe). A hot pot of scallops and maitake mushrooms simmered in a nutty sesame-miso broth, named for the tea master Sen no Rikyū who favored sesame in his cooking; finished with a drizzle of ground sesame paste and a dab of karashi mustard on the side.

Dish: Camarones en Adobo Rojo de Guajillo con Tortillas de Maíz. A Veracruz-style dish of shrimp marinated in a smoky red adobo of guajillo and ancho chiles, achiote, garlic, and bitter orange, then seared and served with warm corn tortillas and pickled red onion.
Dish: Bacalao al Ajoarriero con Almendras. Salt cod simmered with garlic, choricero peppers, tomato, and potatoes in an Aragonese-style ajoarriero sauce, finished with toasted almonds and parsley.

Dish: Tlayuda de Chapulines. A crisp, oven-toasted giant corn tortilla layered with refried black beans, stringy Oaxaca quesillo, toasted chapulines (chile-lime seasoned grasshoppers), avocado, and a smoky chile pasilla salsa.
Dish: Bánh Canh Ghẹ Rang Muối Hội An. Chewy tapioca-rice noodles in a rich crab broth, topped with a whole salt-and-pepper roasted crab, scallion oil, and crispy shallots.

Dish: 鯖の柚庵焼き (Saba no Yuzuan-yaki). Mackerel fillets marinated in a yuzu-scented soy sauce, mirin, and sake mixture, then grilled over charcoal until the skin is lightly charred and the citrus glaze caramelizes.

Dish: น้ำพริกมะขามกุ้งย่าง. A tangy-sweet Thai chili paste (nam prik) made from tamarind pulp, palm sugar, fish sauce, shrimp paste, garlic, shallots, and dried chilies, served with grilled prawns, steamed jasmine rice, and an assortment of fresh and blanched vegetables for dipping.

Dish: तिल-बादाम कोफ्ता करी (Til-Badam Kofta Curry). Deep-fried dumplings of paneer, crushed almonds, and toasted sesame seeds, simmered in a saffron-cashew gravy; a Hyderabadi-influenced festive dish.

Dish: Cazuela de Rape y Almejas al Azafrán ("Saffron Monkfish and Clam Stew"). A Cantabrian coastal stew of monkfish and clams simmered in a saffron-and-white-wine broth with a sofrito of onion, garlic and tomato, thickened at the end with a picada of toasted almonds and fried bread, and finished with parsley.
Dish: Ganjang Gejang.
Dish: Moo Grob Pad Prik King Bai Makrut. Crispy pork belly wok-tossed with red curry paste, green beans, and torn kaffir lime leaves, finished with a fiery Thai chili kick.
Dish: Zarzuela de Marisco. A festive Catalan seafood stew of monkfish, prawns, mussels, and squid simmered in a saffron-brandy tomato sofrito, finished with a garlic-almond-fried-bread picada.
Dish: Chiles en Nogada.
Dish: Mahshi Malfouf bil Loz. Cabbage leaves stuffed with spiced lamb, rice, and toasted almonds, gently simmered in a tangy pomegranate-tamarind broth.
Dish: Kani Miso Chawanmushi. A silky steamed egg custard enriched with sweet crab roe paste and bonito dashi, finished with a sliver of shiitake and mitsuba leaf.
Dish: Har Gow.

Dish: Bún Tôm Nướng Sả Ớt Chấm Mắm Gừng. A central Vietnamese-style rice vermicelli dish topped with lemongrass-and-chili-marinated grilled shrimp, fresh herbs, pickled carrot and daikon, crushed roasted peanuts, and fried shallots, served with a tangy ginger-spiked fish sauce dressing for drizzling or dipping.
Dish: Fabada Asturiana.
Dish: Larb Pla Duk Grob. Crispy shredded catfish tossed Isaan-style with toasted rice powder, lime juice, chilies, mint, and shallots.

Dish: Cazuela de Rape y Almejas al Azafrán. An Andalusian coastal stew of monkfish and clams simmered in a saffron-infused broth with a garlic-almond-fried bread picada, olive oil, and a splash of white wine.
Dish: ስጋ ወጥ (Sega Wat). A rich, slow-cooked Ethiopian beef stew simmered in berbere spice and niter kibbeh (spiced clarified butter), served atop injera flatbread.

Dish: የበሶ ፍርፍር በቅቤ (Yebeso Firfir Beqibe). Torn injera tossed with toasted beso (roasted barley and legume flour), simmered in niter kibbeh (spiced clarified butter) with berbere, shallots, and garlic; a warming breakfast or fasting-adjacent dish from the Ethiopian highlands.
Dish: Bún Riêu Cua. A hearty Hanoi-style rice noodle soup in a tangy tomato-crab broth, topped with silky tofu, minced pork, fresh herbs, and a dab of fermented shrimp paste.

Dish: Tourton de Sarrasin aux Escargots du Vercors et Beurre Persillé. A half-moon buckwheat-and-wheat pastry turnover from the Vercors massif, filled with land snails braised in white wine and stuffed with garlic-parsley butter, brushed with egg wash before baking.
Dish: Nilgiri Murgh Korma. Chicken simmered in a pale green sauce of pureed mint, coriander, green chilies, coconut, and cashews, a specialty of the hill-station kitchens of the Nilgiri range.

Dish: The Blue Plate Reuben Hash. A cast-iron skillet of crispy hash browns piled with slow-braised corned beef, tangy sauerkraut, and melted Swiss, topped with a fried egg and a drizzle of Thousand Island dressing.
Dish: Bún riêu.

Dish: አሳ ክትፎ (Asa Ketfo). A Lake Tana specialty: finely minced fresh tilapia hand-tossed (traditionally raw or barely warmed) in niter kibbeh spiced with mitmita and cardamom, served alongside ayib (fresh crumbled cheese) and sautéed gomen greens, eaten with injera -- a riverine reinterpretation of the classic beef kitfo.
Dish: Baingan ka Salan.
Dish: Ossobuco alla Milanese.
Dish: Jiu Wong Zheng Ban Yu Juan (酒皇蒸斑柳卷). Delicate rolls of garoupa fillet steamed with Shaoxing wine, ginger, and scallion, finished with a light soy-infused broth.
Dish: Shish Barak. Tiny meat-filled dumplings simmered in a garlicky yogurt sauce, finished with sizzling ghee, toasted pine nuts, and fresh mint.

Dish: Yuxiang Shanji Bao (鱼香山鸡煲). Free-range chicken thigh braised in a tangy 'fish-fragrant' sauce of pickled chilies, garlic, ginger and black vinegar, simmered clay-pot style with wood ear mushrooms and scallions.
Dish: Kibbet Batata Malikiyya. Crisp potato-and-bulgur shells stuffed with spiced ground lamb, pine nuts, and caramelized onions, finished with a tangy lemon-tahini drizzle.
Dish: Asa Bicha Wat. A gently spiced Ethiopian fish stew simmered in a golden turmeric-onion sauce, served with injera for scooping.

Dish: Beignets de moelle en croûte, sauce au vin jaune et noisettes torréfiées. Crusted beef bone marrow fritters from the Jura region, served with a vin jaune cream sauce and toasted hazelnuts. English: 'Crusted bone marrow fritters with vin jaune sauce and toasted hazelnuts.'.
Dish: Vincisgrassi alla Maceratese. A rustic Marche-style baked lasagna layering delicate egg pasta sheets with a rich chicken liver and prosciutto ragù, béchamel, and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Dish: Reuben Sandwich.

Dish: 麻辣脆皮兔柳 (Málà Cuìpí Tùliǔ). Sichuan-style crispy-fried rabbit fillet strips, marinated in egg white and Shaoxing wine, double-fried until crackling, then tossed in a fiery mala sauce of dried chilies, Sichuan peppercorns, doubanjiang, garlic and scallions, finished with toasted peanuts and sesame seeds.
Dish: 水煮牛肉 (Shuǐzhǔ Niúròu / Water-Boiled Beef).

Dish: ยำปลาดุกฟูมะม่วงใบชะพลู (Yam Pla Duk Fu Mamuang Bai Cha Phlu). A Thai salad of deep-fried, shredded crispy catfish tossed with shredded green mango, wild betel leaves, shallots, roasted crushed peanuts, and a spicy-sour lime-chili-fish sauce dressing.
Dish: Saba Shioyaki.
Dish: Buri Daikon Nabe. A simmering hotpot of tender yellowtail and slow-braised daikon radish in a soy-dashi broth, finished with scallions and a dusting of shichimi pepper.
Dish: Musakhan.

Dish: ลาบปลาดุกกรอบสมุนไพร (Larb Pla Duk Krob Samunphrai). Crispy fried catfish flaked and tossed in a northeastern Thai (Isan) larb dressing of lime juice, fish sauce, toasted rice powder, dried chili, shallots, and fresh mint and cilantro.
Dish: Patty Melt.
Dish: Mole Negro Oaxaqueño con Pollo. Tender chicken simmered in a deep, complex Oaxacan black mole made from charred chiles, toasted nuts and seeds, and a whisper of Mexican chocolate.

Dish: Mixiotes de Conejo en Adobo de Chile Pasilla Mixe. Rabbit pieces marinated in a smoky adobo of toasted pasilla mixe chiles, garlic, and spices, wrapped in parchment (traditionally maguey leaf) and steamed until tender, served with warm corn tortillas.
Dish: Mapo Tofu.

Dish: 折耳根拌牛肚丝 (Zhé'ěrgēn Bàn Niúdǔ Sī). A classic Sichuan cold dish: thinly sliced blanched beef tripe tossed with fresh houttuynia root (fish mint), garlic, chili oil, Sichuan peppercorn oil, and a splash of black vinegar, finished with crushed peanuts and scallion.

Dish: 欖角豆豉蒸鯪魚球 (Laam Gok Dau Si Jing Leng Yu Kau). Steamed dace fish balls with fermented black beans and preserved olive relish, a home-style Cantonese steamed dish often finished with scallion and a drizzle of hot oil.
Dish: Cacio e Pepe.
Dish: Cochinita Pibil.
